utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Madam Registrar, could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-05-87/1-A, the Prosecutor versus Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now why is this not working? I can't hear anything. Let me see if it's the volume. All right. Okay. Thank you. Appearances. Let's start with the Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honour. Kyle Wood and Christine Dahl for the Prosecution, along with our case manager, Colin Nawrot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, and welcome to this Status Conference. Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Veljko Djurdjic as Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And good morning to you and welcome to this Status Conference. Before we proceed any further, I would like to make sure that everyone can follow the proceedings in a language they understand. And of course in particular, I refer myself to you, Mr. Djordjevic. Are you able to follow the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So this Status Conference is called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal. As you know, Rule 65 bis (B) requires a Status Conference to be convened every 120 days after the filing of a notice of appeal, and thereafter within 120 days after the last Status Conference. The purpose is to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. In the present appeal, the parties filed the notices of appeal on 24th May 2011, and the first Status Conference was held on the 30th of May of last year. The second and third Status Conferences were held on 21st September 2011 and 16th January 2012 respectively. Today's Status Conference being the fourth in this case was scheduled by an order issued by me on 29th March 2012. The first topic I'm going to deal with is the detention conditions and health of appellant Djordjevic. Mr. Djordjevic, if you have any concerns in relation to the conditions of your detention or your state of health, I would invite you to raise them now; and if you prefer, this discussion can proceed in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything is fine, Your Honour. I have no concerns at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Djordjevic. Yes, I will proceed with giving an account, a short account, of the recent procedural history in this case. And I know that this is information that you are aware of, but one of the purposes of the Status Conference is also to make public the recent developments in this case. Before everything else, then, I would say that on the 11th March 2011, the parties were granted an extension of time of 60 days to file their notices of appeal. Both parties filed their respective notices of appeal on 24th May 2011. The Prosecution presented two grounds of appeal and Djordjevic presented 19 grounds of appeal. On the 27th May of last year, the Djordjevic Defence filed a motion requesting an extension of time and word limit in respect of its appeal brief. At the Status Conference of 30th May 2011, I extended the dead-line for filing appeal briefs by seven days to 15th August 2011 for both parties. In addition, I granted the Djordjevic Defence an extension of up to 15.000 words for its appeal brief and granted the Prosecution the same extension in respect of its brief in response. Both parties filed their appeal briefs on 15th August 2011. At the Status Conference held on the 21st September 2011, the Djordjevic Defence team requested an extension of time of 15 days for the filing of its reply brief as well as an extension of the word limit by 6.000 words. I granted both parties an extension of time till 26th October 2011 for the filing of their briefs and reply and also granted the Djordjevic Defence team an extension of up to 3.000 words. Both parties filed their response briefs on 26th September 2011 and subsequently filed their reply briefs on 26th October 2011. As requested by myself, the Prosecution filed a public redacted version of its appeal brief on 17th August 2011. Similarly, on 30th September 2011, the Djordjevic Defence team filed its public redacted version. This was later withheld pending determination of a confidential motion filed on 24th November 2011 by the Prosecution, in which it requested the redaction of certain information from Djordjevic's appeal brief. The Djordjevic Defence filed its confidential response to the motion on 7th December of last year and the Prosecution filed its confidential reply two days later on the 9th of December of last year. I issued a confidential decision on this matter in my capacity as pre-Appeal Judge on 20 January 2012, and in that decision I granted the Prosecution motion in part and ordered, inter alia, Djordjevic to file a new public redacted version of his appeal brief, incorporating one additional redaction. Pursuant to that decision, appellant Djordjevic re-filed the public redacted version of this appeal brief on 23rd January of this year. Both parties filed public redacted versions of their response briefs on 30th January 2012. The Prosecution filed its public redacted reply brief on 8 February 2012 and appellant Djordjevic filed a notice of re-classification of his reply brief on 9th February 2012. Finally, in case any one of you is not aware of this, I note that on the 7th of March of this year the Tribunal's President, President Meron, issued an order replacing a Judge in this appeal. Pursuant to that order, Judge Khalida Rachid Khan was assigned to the Bench in place of Judge Fausto Pocar. So that's the procedural history. Having said this I'll move to the next matter on the issue, on the agenda, and that is any issue that the parties might wish to raise, and I start with the Prosecution. Is there any matter that you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Djurdjic, any matter that you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And appellant Djordjevic, is there anything that you wish to state? Any matter that you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Before I conclude I just wanted to inform you that the Chamber is working hard on this case and is pretty well advanced in its preparation for the hearing. My anticipation is that we will soon have our documentation in preparation of the hearing ready. We'll go through it, me and my colleagues, before we set a day for the hearing of the appeal. I anticipate that to happen either very late this year or early next year. Thank you. This concludes today's Status Conference. I take this opportunity to thank you all for your attendance and now adjourn this session. Thank you.
